 Curfews, Property Tax Deadlines and New Travel Links: News Digest
 First published: 20th October 2026
 by 
 Sophie Lee
 By Sophie Lee 
 France is facing renewed unrest following demonstrations over the cost of living and public services, with local curfews introduced in several cities. Meanwhile, property owners face an online tax payment deadline today, President Emmanuel Macron has secured additional diesel supplies from Gulf states, France’s newest motorway is preparing to open, and airlines are adding new routes for the winter season. Here are the headlines you need to know about France this week.
 French Property Owners: Online Tax Deadline Is Today
 Property owners in France who are liable for taxe foncière (the annual property ownership tax) have until midnight on 20 October to pay online via the French tax website or mobile app. This includes owners who rent out their properties. The amount will be debited from their bank account from 26 October, with the exact date confirmed when payment is registered. The deadline for those paying by other permitted methods was 15 October.
 Curfews introduced after violent demonstrations across France
 French authorities have introduced localised overnight curfews following violent demonstrations across the country over the weekend. Clashes, looting and damage to shops and public buildings were reported in cities including Paris, Lyon and Marseille, prompting the government to review security measures.
 Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said the targeted curfews helped restore calm overnight on Monday and that further restrictions could be introduced where necessary. The demonstrations began with students protesting against deteriorating school conditions but have broadened into wider expressions of anger over the cost of living and public services.
 Further demonstrations are expected on Saturday, 24 October. Residents should check local announcements for possible restrictions and disruption to public transport, particularly in larger cities.
 Businesses assess damage following weekend unrest
 Businesses across France are assessing the damage after widespread looting and vandalism during the weekend demonstrations. Shops, supermarkets, banks and other businesses were among those affected, with concerns about the financial impact on local retailers and small businesses.
 The government faces pressure to support affected businesses as they deal with repairs, insurance claims and lost trading. The unrest has also affected cultural attractions in Paris, with protesters blocking the entrance to the Louvre on Monday, resulting in disruption for visitors.
 The incidents highlight the potential impact of continued demonstrations on everyday life, businesses and tourism.
 Macron secures additional diesel supplies from Gulf states
 President Emmanuel Macron has secured commitments for an additional 200,000 tonnes of diesel per month from the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain, according to the Élysée Palace. The announcement came during a diplomatic tour of the Gulf as France faces pressure from rising fuel costs and concerns over international energy supplies.
 The additional supplies are intended to strengthen France’s access to diesel at a time when disruption to international oil transport has heightened concerns about energy security. However, it remains unclear how quickly the additional deliveries will affect fuel availability and prices at French petrol stations.
 Fuel costs have become a central concern for households and businesses, particularly those reliant on cars and road transport.
 2027 budget proposes tax changes for furnished holiday rentals
 The French government’s draft 2027 budget proposes further changes to the tax treatment of furnished rental properties, with holiday lets facing tighter restrictions on deductions. Under the proposed measures, non-professional furnished landlords using the actual expenses tax regime would face a cap on property depreciation deductions of 2.5% of the property’s value, up to €7,000 per household each year. For furnished tourist accommodation, the proposed limit is lower, at 1.5% and €5,000 annually.
 The plans also seek to prevent landlords from carrying forward unused depreciation deductions from 2027 onwards, while increasing penalties for rental platforms that fail to report users’ income to the authorities. The government says the changes are intended to bring the taxation of furnished and unfurnished rentals closer together and encourage longer-term letting.
 The proposals could affect owners who rent out French properties as holiday accommodation, including those using platforms such as Airbnb. However, the measures are part of the draft Finance Bill for 2027 and may change as the legislation progresses through Parliament.
 A69 motorway set to open between Toulouse and Castres
 France’s newest motorway, the A69, is nearing its long-awaited opening in south-west France. The 62km route will connect Toulouse with Castres in the Tarn department, giving the town a direct motorway link and potentially reducing journey times for motorists.
 The project has been controversial, facing sustained opposition from environmental campaigners and legal challenges over its construction. Supporters argue that the road will improve regional transport links and benefit local businesses, while opponents have raised concerns about its environmental impact.
 Drivers planning to use the new route should check the latest opening announcements and toll arrangements before travelling.
 New winter flight routes announced from France
 Airlines are introducing new routes as their autumn and winter schedules take effect, offering travellers in France additional options for trips across Europe and further afield.
 The new services include connections to destinations in Europe, North Africa and North America, with routes varying by departure airport and airline. The changes may be useful for residents planning winter holidays or visits to family abroad, particularly around the Toussaint and Christmas school holidays.
 Travellers should check flight dates and operating schedules directly with airlines, as some routes will run seasonally rather than throughout the year.
 French mortgage rates edge towards 4%
 Mortgage borrowing costs in France have continued to rise since the beginning of September, with some rates approaching 4%, according to recent figures reported by French financial and property publications.
 Although the increases remain more moderate than those seen during the 2022 interest rate shock, higher borrowing costs can affect how much prospective buyers are able to borrow and the overall cost of purchasing a property.
 For anyone planning to buy a home in France, it is worth comparing offers from several lenders and factoring borrowing costs into the budget before making an offer.
 Just over three months to go until the French Property Exhibition
 Planning to buy a home in France? The French Property Exhibition returns to London on 23–24 January 2027, bringing together estate agents, property experts and specialists in French tax, legal matters, mortgages, currency exchange and relocation. Visitors can browse properties for sale across France, speak to experts face to face and attend free seminars covering the buying process and moving to France. Entry is free, with tickets available through the official French Property Exhibition website .
